description:
## Empirical anchor

Arc 39 CATO finding C1 (2026-05-18, post-CATO Phase 3 review). CATO probe deployed substrate/skills/save-verdict/ to a fresh temp dir via install.sh and observed __pycache__/ + *.pyc files copied into target _lib/__pycache__/ when the source-side worktree had run the helper at least once.

## Failure mode

install.sh uses `cp -R` to deploy skill directories. cp -R has no native exclude mechanism. If the operator runs the deployed helper locally before install.sh runs (developer/operator workflow), the source worktree accumulates __pycache__/. install.sh then copies that pycache into every target tier. Practical impact is benign — pycache regenerates automatically on import — but it pollutes target trees with bytecode the consumer didn't author.

## Why not fixed in Arc 39

Per CLAUDE.md global Fix-now "legitimate reasons to defer" #2: the fix touches install.sh deploy mechanism (not just a wiring add), introduces a new find+rm step that needs platform-portability testing across Windows Git Bash + macOS + Linux, would need a design or A-LOCKED disposition. Bundling would mix scopes with the save-verdict-promotion + ezj-canon arc and slightly degrade reviewability. Source-side .gitignore __pycache__/+*.pyc was added in Arc 39 commit f707bc6 (prevents accidental commit; orthogonal to deploy-side filtering).

Also: the defect surfaces only when developer/operator runs the helper THEN runs install.sh on same working tree. Fresh-clone → install.sh path is unaffected. Lower-risk than a fresh-clone bug.

## Concrete next-step plan

1. Decide implementation:
   - **(α)** Post-copy cleanup: install.sh runs `find <target>/<skill-name> -name __pycache__ -type d -exec rm -rf {} +` after each cp -R. Works on Windows Git Bash + macOS + Linux (find -name is portable; rm -rf is portable). Adds 1 line per deploy loop.
   - **(β)** Pre-copy cleanup: install.sh runs the same find against the SOURCE before cp -R. Same line cost; cleans source side; risks operator surprise if source pycache was load-bearing for some reason.
   - **(γ)** Filtered copy: use `rsync --exclude='__pycache__' --exclude='*.pyc'` instead of cp -R. NOT portable — rsync is not universal on Windows Git Bash deployments.
   
   PLINY-lean: (α) post-copy cleanup. Targets deploy artifact only (orthogonal to source); portable; 1 line per loop.

2. Author probe: deploy save-verdict from a worktree that has populated __pycache__/, verify target tier's deployed _lib/ does NOT contain __pycache__/ or *.pyc.

3. Run smoke beats per Arc 23 §8.4 substrate-edit smoke-beat discipline: install.sh --dry-run at all 3 tiers should NOT show __pycache__ in deploy plan after fix.

4. Update install.sh deploy loop. Run probe. Commit per §28 trailer + §5.10 verified signoff.

5. Bundle into next available arc (Arc 40 candidate addition; or separate small-scope arc).

## Out of scope

- Refactoring install.sh's broader deploy mechanism (replacing cp -R wholesale)
- Filtering for non-Python artifacts (.DS_Store, *.swp, etc.) — separate concern, separate ticket if needed

## Cross-references

- Arc 39 commit f707bc6 (source-side .gitignore __pycache__/+*.pyc add)
- Arc 39 CATO verdict at agents/verdicts/arc-39/CAPTAIN_CATO-2026-05-18T06-30-00Z.md (C1 finding)
- Arc 39 build commits 519226e..arc-39/build HEAD
- stoa--sp1 (port 7-8 cross-substrate utility skills) — when sp1 promotes copy-artifact + transcribe-bw-to-disk (the other 2 Python skills the cross-skill share at A2-β considered), the same deploy-side filtering applies to those too. Bundling sp1 + this ticket together saves a deploy-loop touch.

## Sequencing

P3. Next-arc candidate. Fix-now with concrete plan per CLAUDE.md global. Not blocking Arc 40 substrate work.
title: install.sh deploy excludes __pycache__/ when copying Python substrate skills
